content:
Marketing a residential project in Pune comes down to two things done properly: every advertisement, from a hoarding to a WhatsApp forward, carries the project's MahaRERA registration number, the regulator's website address and the project QR code where a buyer can actually see them; and every rupee of ad spend is judged by site visits and bookings, not by the number of "leads" in a spreadsheet. As a digital marketing agency in Pune, we see builders lose money on both sides: creatives that have to be pulled because the RERA details are missing or unreadable, and campaigns that deliver 800 form fills of which the sales team can reach 150.

This guide is for developers, their marketing heads and channel-partner managers selling apartments, plots and commercial space in Pune, Pimpri-Chinchwad and the rest of Maharashtra. It covers what MahaRERA expects in advertisements, how to build a project landing page, how to choose between Meta lead forms, landing pages and Google Search, how to qualify and follow up leads, and how to measure cost per site visit. It is not legal advice; confirm the current MahaRERA orders and circulars with your compliance team, because the regulator updates them.

## What MahaRERA requires in project advertisements

Three layers of rules apply to any advertisement for a project that needs registration.

### The Act: registration number and website address

Under the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016, a promoter may not advertise, market, book or sell in a project that requires registration until it is registered (section 3), and every advertisement or prospectus must mention prominently the website address of the Authority and the registration number (section 11(2)).

### The 2023 order: the QR code

MahaRERA generates a QR code for each registered project; scanning it opens the project's page on the MahaRERA portal with the registration details, sanctioned plans, completion date and updates. By Order No. 46/2023 dated 29 May 2023, MahaRERA directed promoters to display that QR code prominently on every project advertisement from 1 August 2023, beside the registration number and the MahaRERA website address, in a form that is legible and can be detected by scanning software. A follow-up order set the penalty: a minimum of ₹10,000, extendable up to ₹50,000, for each violation.

### The April 2025 circular: where and how large

Because the details were often printed in tiny type or pale colours, MahaRERA issued a circular in April 2025 tightening the presentation. As reported at the time, it requires:

- the MahaRERA registration number, the MahaRERA website address and the QR code to be displayed **prominently**;
- in a **font size at least as large as the project's contact details** in the advertisement;
- in the **top-right portion** of the advertisement, in a colour that stands out from the background;
- across **every medium**: newspapers, leaflets, brochures, hoardings, electronic media, banners, websites, social media, and messages sent through WhatsApp and similar services.

Reports of the circular state that a promoter may be fined up to ₹50,000 and is given ten days to correct the advertisement, with continued non-compliance treated as a further violation.

### It is enforced

MahaRERA has repeatedly published enforcement figures; in mid-2024 it reported action against 628 projects for advertising without the registration number or QR code. It has also tied up with the Advertising Standards Council of India (ASCI) to monitor advertisements, including digital ones. Orders have gone against promoters who argued that the advertisement was simply too small for the details to be readable.

### Agents and channel partners

Real estate agents must themselves be registered with MahaRERA, and creatives circulated by channel partners for your project are still advertisements for your project. Treat partner creatives as part of your compliance scope: give partners approved templates and do not let them make their own.

## Turning the rule into a creative checklist

The rule is simple; the failures are operational. A designer resizes a hoarding into an Instagram story and crops the corner with the QR code. A sales executive forwards a price sheet on WhatsApp with no RERA number. Build the checks into production.

**For every static creative (print, hoarding, social post, display banner):**

- RERA block in the top-right: registration number, `maharera.maharashtra.gov.in` (confirm the current official address), QR code.
- Text in the RERA block is no smaller than the phone number or website on the same creative.
- The QR code has a clear margin around it and enough contrast; test it by scanning the final exported file on two phones, not the design file.
- One master template per project with the RERA block locked, so that resizing cannot remove it.

**For small formats (Instagram stories, 300×250 banners, WhatsApp images):**

- Design the small format from scratch rather than shrinking the large one. If the QR code cannot be scanned at the size the viewer will see, the creative is not compliant; simplify the rest of the creative instead of shrinking the RERA block.

**For video and reels:**

- Show the RERA block on screen long enough to read and scan. A sensible working rule is to keep it visible throughout, in the top-right, or at the least on the opening and end frames for several seconds. (The orders we have read do not specify a duration; ask your compliance team for a house rule.)

**For text ads and captions (Google Search ads, post captions, SMS, WhatsApp text):**

- A search ad cannot carry a QR code. Include the registration number in the ad text where the format allows, and make sure the landing page shows the full RERA block at the top. Put the registration number and MahaRERA address in every caption and message template.

**For projects with several phases or wings:**

- Each registered phase has its own number and QR code. An advertisement for Tower C must carry Tower C's details, and a creative covering the whole township needs all the relevant numbers.

**Before launch:**

- Do not run "pre-launch" or "expression of interest" campaigns for a project that requires registration and does not yet have it. That is advertising an unregistered project.
- Keep an approval log: creative, version, who checked the RERA block, date. If a notice arrives, you will need it.

## The project landing page

Every campaign needs a page that it sends people to. For a project, that page has to do four things: confirm the buyer has found the right project, answer the first five questions, show that the project is registered, and capture the enquiry.

### What goes on it

1. **Top band**: project name, location, configuration and price range, with the RERA number, MahaRERA website address and QR code at the top right.
2. **Key facts**: configurations with carpet area (RERA carpet, in square feet and square metres), price range per configuration, possession date as declared to MahaRERA, number of towers and floors.
3. **Location**: a map, and distances stated as distance or typical drive time with the time of day, not "5 minutes from Hinjawadi".
4. **Floor plans**: one per configuration, downloadable.
5. **Amenities**: what is in this phase, separately from what is planned for later phases.
6. **Construction status**: dated photos, updated monthly.
7. **Price sheet or cost breakdown**: base price, stamp duty and registration, GST where applicable, maintenance deposit, parking. Buyers trust a project that shows the full figure.
8. **Enquiry form and click-to-call**, repeated after the key sections.
9. **Developer details**: completed projects, with their own RERA numbers where applicable.
10. **Disclaimers** in readable type.

### Claims to check against the registration

What you say on the page must match what is registered. Check the possession date, carpet areas, number of units and amenities against the MahaRERA entry. Avoid "assured returns", "guaranteed appreciation" and "pre-approved by all banks" unless you can document each. Label artist's impressions as such, and mark the show flat as a show flat.

### Speed and tracking

Most property traffic is mobile and arrives from Instagram, where patience is short. Keep the page light: compress renders, avoid auto-playing video backgrounds, and load the 3D walkthrough only when tapped. Record form submissions, call clicks, WhatsApp clicks and brochure downloads as separate events in GA4. Our article on [landing pages versus the home page for ads](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-landing-page-vs-homepage-ads-2026) explains why a dedicated page per project and campaign outperforms sending traffic to the corporate site.

## Which channels, and what each is good for

### Google Search: people already looking

Someone searching "2 BHK in Baner under 1 crore" or your project name is far along. Search campaigns usually bring fewer leads at a higher cost per lead than Meta, and a much higher share of them answer the phone.

- Build separate campaigns for **brand and project name**, **location plus configuration**, and **competitor or generic** terms, so you can see which is paying.
- Add negatives early: "rent", "PG", "resale", "jobs", "careers", "MHADA lottery" if not relevant.
- Use location targeting deliberately. NRIs and buyers relocating from other cities matter for Pune, so do not restrict everything to a 10 km radius.
- Portal aggregators bid on your project name. A small brand campaign protects it.

Our [Google Ads service](/services/google-ads) covers this set-up.

### Meta (Facebook and Instagram): creating demand

Meta is where buyers who were not searching discover a project. It produces volume cheaply, and the volume needs filtering.

- **Instant lead forms** are easy to fill, because Meta pre-fills name and phone. That is why they produce many accidental and low-intent leads. Use the "higher intent" form type, which adds a review step, and add two or three qualifying questions.
- **Landing-page campaigns** produce fewer leads that usually know more about the project, since they have read the page first.
- **Click-to-WhatsApp ads** suit buyers who prefer to chat; they work only if someone, or a well-built chatbot, replies immediately.

We compare the first two in detail in [Meta lead ads versus landing pages](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-meta-lead-ads-vs-landing-page-2026). For most projects we would run both and judge them on cost per site visit, which often reverses the ranking that cost per lead suggests. See also our [Meta Ads service](/services/meta-ads).

### Property portals, Google Business Profile and organic social

Portals deliver buyers who are comparing; treat them as a paid channel and track them with the same lead-to-visit measures. Create a Google Business Profile for the site office or sales gallery, with correct timings and photos, since many buyers navigate to it. Organic Instagram and YouTube (construction updates, walkthroughs, locality guides) support the paid work and reassure buyers who look you up; we run this as part of [social media management for real estate](/services/social-media/real-estate).

## Lead quality: qualify at the form, not on the tenth call

A sales team that has to call 800 people to find 40 interested ones stops calling by day three. Filter earlier.

**Qualifying questions that work** (pick two or three, as multiple choice):

- Configuration wanted: 1 BHK / 2 BHK / 3 BHK.
- Budget band: shown as ranges that begin at your real starting price. If the project starts at ₹85 lakh, the lowest option is "₹85 lakh – ₹1 crore", with an honest "Below ₹85 lakh" that routes to a polite message instead of the sales queue.
- When they plan to buy: within 3 months / 3–6 months / just exploring.
- Self-use or investment.
- Preferred time for a call.

**Verify the phone number** with an OTP on landing-page forms. It reduces volume and removes mistyped and fake numbers.

**Send the price range in the first automated reply.** Buyers who are far outside the budget drop out by themselves, which is the point.

**Deduplicate** across Meta, Google, portals and channel partners on phone number, and record the first source, so that two teams do not call the same buyer and the commission question has an answer.

## Speed and follow-up

Property enquiries are made in batches: the buyer fills forms for four projects in one evening. The developer who calls first, with someone who knows the project, usually gets the site visit.

- **Route leads automatically** into a CRM the moment they arrive, assigned to a named executive by project and language. Downloading a CSV from Meta every evening is how leads die.
- **Send an instant WhatsApp or SMS** with the brochure, location pin, RERA number and the executive's name.
- **Call within minutes during working hours**, and first thing in the morning for night-time leads.
- **Follow a fixed sequence**: several call attempts over the first few days at different times, then a message, then a slower nurture (construction updates, offers, a new tower launch). Buying a home takes months; most bookings come from leads older than 30 days.
- **Book the site visit as an appointment** with a date, time and reminder, and record whether it happened.
- **Use WhatsApp templates properly**: opt-in at the form, utility templates for visit confirmations, marketing templates for offers, each carrying the RERA details.

Our guide to [lead response speed and follow-up workflows](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-lead-response-speed-follow-up-workflow-2026) sets out the sequence, and [real estate CRM versus ERP](/blog/real-estate-crm-vs-erp) explains what the CRM should and should not try to do.

## Measurement: cost per site visit, not cost per lead

Track every lead through five stages and report cost at each:

1. Lead received
2. Contacted (spoke to the buyer)
3. Qualified (budget, location and timing fit)
4. Site visit done
5. Booking

A hypothetical month, to show why this matters (illustrative numbers, not benchmarks):

| | Meta instant form | Meta landing page | Google Search |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spend | ₹1,50,000 | ₹1,50,000 | ₹1,50,000 |
| Leads | 600 | 250 | 120 |
| Cost per lead | ₹250 | ₹600 | ₹1,250 |
| Site visits | 12 | 15 | 18 |
| Cost per site visit | ₹12,500 | ₹10,000 | ₹8,333 |

On cost per lead, the instant form wins by a wide margin. On cost per site visit, it comes last, and it also consumed the most calling time. Your own numbers will differ, and may well favour Meta; what matters is that you measure to the visit.

Then feed the result back to the platforms. Upload qualified leads and site visits to Google Ads as offline conversions, and send them to Meta through the Conversions API, so the algorithms optimise for buyers who visit rather than people who tap. Our article on [lead quality and offline conversions](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-lead-quality-offline-conversions-2026) explains the set-up.

Use UTM parameters on every link and a separate tracked phone number or WhatsApp entry point per channel, including hoardings and print. A QR code on a hoarding that leads to a tracked landing page (separate from the MahaRERA QR code, and clearly labelled so buyers know which is which) tells you whether the hoarding is doing anything.

## Budget and what to expect

Property is a high-value, long-cycle purchase. Plan for months, not weeks.

- **Media budget**: developers commonly plan marketing as a small percentage of project revenue, split across launch, sustenance and closing phases. The right figure depends on ticket size, inventory and competition; we do not quote a universal percentage because we have not found a reliable published benchmark for Pune.
- **Cost per lead** varies widely with ticket size and location. Expect premium and commercial projects to cost several times more per lead than affordable housing, and do not compare your figures with another project's without comparing the ticket size.
- **Agency fees** for managing Google and Meta campaigns, landing pages and reporting for one project typically run from about ₹30,000 to ₹1,00,000 a month, plus media spend, depending on scope and number of creatives.
- **Landing page and tracking set-up**: roughly ₹25,000 to ₹80,000 per project, more with a 3D walkthrough or unit-availability viewer.
- **CRM and WhatsApp automation**: depends on the tool and number of users; budget for it, because without it the media spend leaks.

## A 30-day launch plan

- **Days 1–5**: confirm registration details and download the QR code; build master creative templates with the locked RERA block; write the landing page; set up CRM routing and WhatsApp templates.
- **Days 6–10**: publish the page; set up GA4 events, Meta pixel and Conversions API, Google conversion tracking; test every form with a real phone; brief the sales team on the follow-up sequence.
- **Days 11–20**: launch brand and location search campaigns and two Meta approaches (higher-intent form and landing page) with three to four creatives each; review search terms and lead quality every two days.
- **Days 21–30**: compare channels on contacted rate and site visits; pause the weakest creative and form; add remarketing to page visitors; upload the first batch of offline conversions.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is a QR code mandatory in real estate advertisements in Maharashtra?

Yes. MahaRERA's Order No. 46/2023 requires promoters to display the project's MahaRERA QR code prominently on advertisements from 1 August 2023, beside the registration number and the MahaRERA website address. An April 2025 circular added that these details must be prominent, placed at the top right and no smaller than the contact details.

### What is the penalty for not showing the MahaRERA number or QR code in an ad?

MahaRERA's orders provide for a penalty from ₹10,000 up to ₹50,000 for each violation, and the regulator has reported action against hundreds of projects. Reports of the 2025 circular say promoters are given ten days to correct the advertisement, after which continued non-compliance is treated as a further violation.

### Do MahaRERA advertisement rules apply to Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp?

Yes. The requirement covers advertisements in any medium. Reports of the April 2025 circular list newspapers, leaflets, hoardings, electronic media, websites, social media and messages sent through WhatsApp and similar services. Put the RERA block on every creative and the registration number in every caption and message template.

### Which is better for real estate leads, Facebook ads or Google Ads?

They do different jobs. Google Search reaches people already looking and usually gives fewer leads with a higher contact rate. Meta creates demand and gives more leads at a lower cost, with more filtering needed. Run both and compare them on cost per site visit, not cost per lead.

### How can builders improve the quality of leads from Meta ads?

Use the higher-intent form type, add two or three qualifying questions such as configuration, budget band and buying timeline, state the price range in the ad and the first reply, verify phone numbers, call within minutes, and send qualified leads and site visits back to Meta as conversions so that the system optimises for them.
